title: Cross-Model Alignment Faking Comparison: Instruction-Tuned Family Survey

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: broader cross-model alignment faking data reduces overgeneralization risk and provides community reference data. Each link is explicit: more models surveyed means better understanding of which model families are at risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running 4-6 instruction-tuned models through a documented probe. Open-source models are available on HuggingFace, but loading and running multiple large models (Mistral, Qwen, Phi, Gemma) requires GPU access and some infrastructure familiarity. Medium compute helps but beginners will need guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Deliverable is a ranked comparison table, which is clear. However, running the probe across 4-6 models requires substantial setup per model. Within 30 hours if scoped to 3-4 models, but the survey breadth creates risk of scope creep.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
